newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Tofas to cut 1,011 jobs in January - union.
newsitem.headline: Turk Tofas to cut 1,011 jobs in January - union.

text.p: Turkey's leading car maker Tofas Turk Otomobil Fabrikasi will lay off 1,011 workers or 22 percent of its workforce on January 2, 1997, an official from labour union Turk Metal said on Wednesday.

The official from Turk Metal's Bursa branch where Tofas's plant is located, said an agreement in principle was reached with the company to put the 1,011 workers on compulsory leave with half pay from November 22 to January 2, 1997.

"By putting the 1,011 workers on compulsory leave until January 2, 1997, they will earn the right to new (higher) redundancy payments. Those near their retirement will be given priority in layoffs," Turk Metal official told Reuters.

Tofas officials were not immediately available for comment, but in a statement sent to the Istanbul Stock Exchange earlier on Wednesday the company said it planned to begin single work shift at its Bursa plant instead of the current two.

It said falling car demand due to expectations of cheaper car imports following a recent government decree to ease import rules "brought up the subject of a single-shift operation instead of two to the stage of practice".

Tofas added in the statement that talks were under way with Turk Metal to find "the most suitable solution" on how to go ahead with the shift reduction which would involve around 1,000 workers and lead to a 30 percent drop in the plant's production capacity.
Tofas is equally owned by Italian Fiat Spa and leading Turkish industrial group Koc Holding with each holding 37.86 percent stake.
Car and parts producers as well as labour unions in Turkey's automotive sector have been strongly opposing a cabinet decree which went into effect on October 24 to ease car import rules.

The decree allows some three million expatriate Turkish workers in Europe to import cars and machinery of up to four years of age without customs duties, if they deposit a minimum of 50,000 marks for one year at state-owned Ziraat Bank.

Expatriates who open the minimum account by end-1996 will be allowed to bring in one duty free foreign car or 50,000 marks worth of machinery from June 1, 1997. They will also receive 10 percent annual interest on their deposits.
The Anatolian agency reported on Wednesday that such accounts totalling 42 million marks had so far been opened at Ziraat Bank.
The government forecasts 25,000 duty free car imports and an income of 1.25 billion marks from the scheme as part of its two revenue raising packages unveiled since late July.
Turkey's car output plunged 32 percent from a year ago to 17,350 units in October and fell by seven percent to 172,964 in January-October, when compared to the same 1995 period.
